intended_object: The diagonal embedding SO(Q)(ℚ) → SO(Q)(𝔸_f^S) of the rational special orthogonal group into the finite adelic special orthogonal group away from S. The target is the restricted product over primes p ∉ S of SO(Q⊗ℚ_p), restricted with respect to compact open reference subgroups; g goes to (g⊗ℚ_p)_{p∉S}. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body composes two maps. The first is the finite adelic diagonal, g ↦ (specialOrthogonalGroupBaseChange to ℚ_p of g)_p. It lands in the restricted product because of the structure field `U.eventually_orthogonal`, which says every rational point lies in the reference subgroup at almost every prime. The second is `restrictAway S`, which is `RestrictedProduct.mapAlongMonoidHom` along `Subtype.val` with the identity on each factor, so it only drops the coordinates indexed by S. The result has p-component g⊗ℚ_p for each p ∉ S (lemma `awayAdelicSpecialOrthogonalDiagonal_apply`), which is exactly the standard diagonal embedding.

Edge cases: the map is defined for every S. When S contains all primes the target is trivial, and the library assumes a prime outside S only for injectivity, which is correct.

`FiniteDimensional ℚ V` is needed to define SO through the determinant. Working over ℚ instead of a general number field comes from the library's infrastructure (`OrthogonalCompactOpens` is defined for quadratic forms over ℚ), not from this map, which is the natural one in that framework.

I found no Mathlib declaration for this embedding.
